body:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: synth-canary-eu1 failed 5/5 probes within 2m (fanout failure). pd#INC-9142 -> paging dev-sre.

pagerduty: Incident INC-9142 created and routed to dev-sre. First responder: alice. Escalation in 10m if not acknowledged.

alice: Acked. Looking. Seen similar spike last week but hopefully unrelated. Which checks are failing?

ben: All canary probes with path /health/check are getting 504s from the env gateway. Observed from EU1 prober fleet only. Example: `curl -v https://probe-eu1.redwood.net/health/check` -> `504 upstream read timeout`.

jordan: Confirmed. Prober logs show repeated `connect() to 10.12.0.5:443 timed out` from the egress NAT IP pool. Also `socket: too many open files` on some prober workers.

maya: Paging notes: customer-facing endpoints are fine; this is our synthetic prober hitting the edge/gateway. Impact: alert noise and potential blind spot for real regression detection. No customer tickets yet.

devon: I'm scaling down prober fanout to reduce concurrent outbound connections — running:```\nkubectl -n monitoring scale deployment prober-eu1 --replicas=4\nkubectl -n monitoring set env deployment/prober-eu1 PROBER_CONCURRENCY=8\n```

alice: Doing that now. Also routing new probes to eu2 as fallback while we stabilize: updating probe-controller routes.

incident-bot: prober-controller: routing update applied, fallback region = eu2 for synth-checks.

ben: After scale down, connection errors dropped by ~70%. Still seeing intermittent 504s from a subset of edge pods (edge-gw-eu1-*) — looks like outbound NAT exhaustion + file descriptor leak on a specific edge node.

jordan: I'm isolating the edge pod: `kubectl cordon node edge-node-17 && kubectl drain edge-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Will restart the node's gateway pod once drained.

maya: PD note: marking as partial loss of monitoring capability (no customer impact). Updating INC-9142 status and adding mitigation steps.

devon: Restarted gw pod and rotated NAT egress IPs for the node. Observability: after restart, probe success rate back to ~99% in eu1.

alice: Re-enabled original fanout to full after 12m. Running smoke batch of 200 probes across eu1 to verify stability.

jordan: Root cause (prelim): recent prober upgrade last night increased per-worker file descriptor limit but a regression in connection pooling meant some sockets remained in TIME_WAIT longer. Combined with NAT port reuse limits on a hot node, this produced transient exhaustion and 504s.

maya: Action items assigned in the incident: 1) revert faulty connection pooling changes in prober (ben), 2) add egress port exhaustion alert and runbook (jordan), 3) increase monitoring of fd usage per pod (devon), 4) add gradual fanout rollout to prober deploys (alice).

alice: Added notes to the runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/synth-prober-egress (see section "egress exhaustion mitigation").

incident-bot: Incident INC-9142 status: mitigated -> monitoring. No further PD pages. Escalation canceled.

pagerduty: Acknowledgement cleared by alice. Incident placed in postmortem queue.

ben: We'll follow up with a short postmortem and a small config change to reduce default prober concurrency and add exponential backoff to the probe client.

jordan: Leaving a note for next oncall: if you see a canary fanout spike, first step = scale prober down, verify node NAT port metrics (aws_vpc_nat_port_usage), cordon hot node, restart gateway pod, and failover probes to fallback region. I'll add that checklist to the runbook.

maya: Handing off to night oncall (devon) in 20m. If anything regresses re-open INC-9142 or create a new alert. :white_check_mark:
